verdict.rationale: Figma Make's own docs describe prompting an agent in chat to generate a code-backed frontend, then adding a backend to store and manage data, and publishing the app to a custom domain. A community commenter confirms the AI writes React code, so the core prompt-to-app flow is delivered end to end. missing for 10: in-depth documentation of what the backend supports (auth, database, server logic) beyond storing and managing data/content, and independent hands-on corroboration that a working full-stack app results from a natural-language prompt.

support.subject: As a founder, I can describe an app in natural language and get a working full-stack application

citations.quote: Generate and design your frontend in Figma Make, then create a backend to manage your content.
You can also [add a backend](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/32640822050199) to your app to securely store and manage data.
Clarify intent and create a structured, editable plan before generation starts.
You can also assign a custom domain that you own.
Everything you build is code-backed and visually editable, so you can easily jump between code and canvas.
